object_context: Child of H4d1a after the verified first-order same-detector no-go. Fix a smooth projective family f:X->S, s0 in S, a local Hodge-locus branch T through s0 for a flat rational Hodge class alpha, and a fixed central algebraic witness z0 represented by a selected point w0 of a coefficient-safe local witness space W_alpha with projection pi:W_alpha->S and pi(w0)=s0. Determine whether the first-order branch-relative obstruction delta_{1,w0} vanishes on T_{s0}T from source-specific pointed witness geometry. This atom does not address initial algebraicity, higher-Artin lifting, algebraization, or global continuation.
structural_coordinates: root coefficients remain rational; a selected witness may be a signed rational cycle encoded by finite coefficient-safe local Hilbert/Chow branches
the Hodge locus T is base-space data for alpha and does not itself select a witness point in a fiber
the selected witness is pointed data w0 over s0; replacing w0 by another witness changes the deformation problem
existential geometric coverage of T by the projection image is logically distinct from a local lifting branch through w0
first-order pointed liftability is controlled by im(d pi_w0), or by an equivalent source-bound tangent/obstruction interface when that interface is proved
the H4d1a same-detector nonzero-envelope route is retired inside its registered first-order scope
any passage from a base-image statement to selected-witness lifting needs local pointed geometry such as tangent dominance, smoothness/formal smoothness, or another source-specific theorem
first-order tangent dominance is not higher-Artin formal lifting; formal lifting is not algebraization; algebraization is not monodromy-safe global continuation
special complete-intersection/divisor controls cannot be generalized to arbitrary codimension or signed rational combinations without a transfer witness
equivalent_formulations: prove delta_{1,w0}|_{T_{s0}T}=0 in a source-bound tangent-obstruction sequence
prove T_{s0}T subseteq im(d pi_w0) for the exact selected witness point w0 when delta_1 is the associated cokernel obstruction
construct a local witness branch or formally smooth pointed morphism through w0 whose image contains the germ of T
separate 'for nearby s there exists some witness over s' from 'the fixed w0 extends through the infinitesimal direction at s0'
solved_analogues: Nishinou's semiregular-map setting: under the source hypotheses a fixed central map deforms relatively iff its cycle class remains Hodge; this is a pointed chosen-witness positive control
codimension-one Picard/divisor deformation, where the witness category has stronger representability and obstruction control
near_solved_analogues: Kloosterman's complete-intersection hypersurface setting: the Hodge locus is smooth at the central hypersurface and the proof explicitly compares its tangent ideal with flag-Hilbert geometry; this is the main source-bound H4d1b calibration candidate
Pridham's global reduced obstruction theory: a legitimate alternate obstruction representation, but not automatic pointed branch lifting for arbitrary cycles

method_transfers.source_context: Kloosterman flag-Hilbert versus Hodge-locus comparison for complete-intersection cycles on hypersurfaces
method_transfers.method: write Y=sum_i P_i Q_i, identify the Hodge tangent ideal, and compare it with first-order variations of the selected flag (Y,Z)
shared_structure: a selected geometric witness point maps to the deformation base
a Hodge-locus germ lives in the same base
explicit tangent equations can test whether every Hodge direction is induced by deforming the selected witness
required_assumptions: the complete-intersection/hypersurface and degree hypotheses hold
the selected flag point (Y,Z) is the witness under study
the tangent-image equality is derived from the exact source equations rather than from image containment alone
disanalogies: the rational Hodge root permits arbitrary codimension and signed rational combinations
the explicit ideal presentation P_i,Q_i is special and has no automatic analogue for a general witness
method_transfers.repair_question: Does Kloosterman's explicit ideal calculation certify im(d pi_(Y,Z)) = T_Y NL([Z]_prim) at the selected flag point, giving a source-bound direct first-order vanishing control without using detector injectivity as the inference step?

method_transfers.source_context: Nishinou relative deformation of semiregular maps with divisor image
method_transfers.method: bind the obstruction to the fixed central map and use semiregularity plus Hodge persistence to obtain relative deformation of that same map
shared_structure: ambient directions create a geometric lifting obstruction
Hodge persistence is compared with pointed obstruction vanishing
required_assumptions: the Hodge class is the one carried by the fixed map
scope is not enlarged beyond the theorem
disanalogies: semiregularity is the strong detector condition H4d1b is trying not to assume generally
the main setup concerns maps with divisor image rather than arbitrary rational cycles
method_transfers.repair_question: Can explicit witness-incidence geometry certify the pointed tangent inclusion without assuming full semiregularity?

method_transfers.source_context: Pridham derived semiregularity and reduced obstruction theory
method_transfers.method: change/reduce the obstruction object through a source-defined derived morphism rather than post-hoc quotienting the detector kernel
shared_structure: a reduced obstruction theory can be fixed functorially
required_assumptions: the derived moduli functor applies to the chosen witness category
the reduced object is fixed before the lifting conclusion
compatibility with T and w0 is separately proved
disanalogies: reduced obstruction theory alone does not prove T_{s0}T subseteq im(d pi_w0)
quotienting by the old detector kernel after H4d1a would erase rather than solve the registered obstruction
method_transfers.repair_question: Can a source-defined reduced object give a non-circular pointed lifting criterion with an auditable map back to the original witness problem?

explicit_disanalogies: Hodge-locus membership is not witness existence, and witness existence is not automatically deformation of the selected witness
image coverage of a morphism does not generally imply surjectivity of its differential at a selected point
smoothness of the Hodge locus does not imply smoothness/formal smoothness of the witness projection
first-order tangent inclusion does not prove higher-Artin lifting
formal lifting does not supply algebraization or global continuation
the previous same-detector impossibility cannot be bypassed by renaming a quotient obstruction object
